consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is spiritual/moral darkness (sin, evil, unbelief, separation from God), contrasted with day/light as God/Christ/truth/salvation; common alternatives include the present evil age before Christ's return, seasons of trial/suffering, death/lost opportunity, and (less centrally) times of prayer/revelation or rest.
book_summary: Night is the absence of Day and Light (defined as visible obedience), marked by sleep or death and by sinful deeds concealed in darkness; at largest scale it is the period from the fall of man until the Kingdom of God begins on earth (opposite: Day).
consensus_core_identification: Spiritual/moral darkness associated with sin, evil, unbelief, and separation from God (foil to day/light).
book_core_identification: Absence of Day/Light (= visible obedience), marked by sleep/death and concealed sinful deeds; cosmically the age from Fall to Kingdom.
boundary_disagreement: Book treats the Fall-to-Kingdom age and the markers of sleep/death/concealed sin as definitional (with Light fixed as visible obedience), whereas consensus keeps the moral-darkness core broader and lists the eschatological age and related markers only as common alternatives or applications.
rationale: Minimum cores share the same darkness-vs-light/sin referent and do not contradict; the book preserves that category while tightening precision (Light = visible obedience) and re-centering the large-scale historical period plus sleep/death/concealed-sin markers as intrinsic rather than secondary, producing a narrower extension of the same core.
strongest_objection: Defining Light strictly as 'visible obedience' and elevating the Fall-to-Kingdom period to the primary large-scale sense may over-specify beyond the multivalent NT dualism that consensus treats as settled.
